items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: So it was a really great experience to come up with my father, you know, learning music in Crowley, Louisiana of all places, the Cajun influence, the Zydeco influence, and my mom learning to play the piano, playing Beethoven and playing Schubert and Chopin, which are some of her favorite composers.

ctx.x: I was talking to Clyde Kerr just now about the family tradition in New Orleans. It’s unbelievable to me, the number of families. It’s almost like a family that would always have carpenters or bricklayers or some families have musicians.

That’s an interesting analogy. I’ve never really thought of it that way. You know I guess in certain areas of the country where certain livelihoods or occupations would dominate, and obviously in New Orleans the music has always been a dominant influence in terms of our culture. And I think that’s one of the reasons why families have evolved so, because outside of my family, the Jordan family, were my mom grew up in a family of 16 kids, if you can believe that, but everybody played an instrument or sang. So it…

You know when you see promo written about people, if you’re from New York or you’re from New Orleans, most likely the promoter or the people who write that copy are going to mention that, especially if you’re playing out of town. Does it mean something to you? Do you think it’s important that you’re from New Orleans as far as the way you play?
